**Meeting**
Troy Board of Education regular meeting, April 16, 2024, Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. Called to order by President Schmidt at 7:00 p.m.; adjourned at 8:42 p.m. Minutes submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary (GH/jh).

**Attendance**
Present with Mr. Schmidt: Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present: Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Smotherman, Keyser, Pagel, Morse, Milanov, Keen, Pawlus, Hall, and West. Approximately 180 members of the audience attended.

**Recognition — Outstanding Teachers**
The District received 48 nominations, resulting in recognition of 41 outstanding teachers. All nominees were honored at a reception on Tuesday, April 9th at Troy High School and received a certificate, their nomination packets, and a token of appreciation; a video of the surprise classroom visits was shown. The top four were honored at the meeting:

| Teacher | Award | School |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Elizabeth Neuville | Preschool Teacher of the Year | TSD Preschool |
| Danielle Davenport | Elementary Teacher of the Year | Hill Elementary School |
| Eric Flessa | High School Teacher of the Year | Troy College & Career High School |
| Stephanie Hyska | Middle School Teacher of the Year and overall TSD Teacher of the Year | Boulan Park Middle School |

All winners were forwarded to Oakland Schools for the Countywide Outstanding Teacher Award program.

**Mission Moment — Autism Acceptance Month**
Moved by Dr. Wilson, supported by Mrs. Alic, a resolution recognizing April 2024 as Autism Acceptance Month in the Troy School District. Whereas clauses noted that Autism Spectrum Disorder affects more than five million people in the United States and that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention report 1 in 36 children may have autism. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Student Spotlight and Volunteer Appreciation**
Mr. Thomas Butcher presented Cassandra Wilson, an Athens High School senior, recognized with a certificate for her TSD Creative Guild work. For Volunteer Appreciation Month the Board honored volunteers whose students graduate from TSD this year: Marti Steiner, Peggy Chinoski, Colleen Geyer, and Tara Colussi.

**Additions & Deletions / Public Communication (Agenda Items) / Personnel / Curriculum / Other**
None.

**Consent Agenda**
Moved by Mr. Hauff, supported by Mr. Haupt, to approve items A through F: minutes of the March 5, 2024 Special Meeting, Closed Session Meeting, and Board Workshop; minutes of the March 19, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report – February 2024; and Ancillary Fund(s) Budget Amendment. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Business — Smith Switch Gear**
Moved by Mrs. Alic, supported by Dr. Philippart, that the bid for the Smith Middle School Switchgear Package be awarded to Great Lakes Power and Lighting in an amount not to exceed $405,000.00, approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. Vote: Yes 7, No 0.

**Public Communication (Non-Agenda Items)**
Jordan Holsbeke (Martell teacher, 2022 Teacher of the Year), Jason Cichowicz (Troy Education Association president), Jacqueline Ciolek (Troy High), Jennifer Lee (Larson Middle School, 26-year teacher), Heather Kelly (Troy High), Jessica Craft (Troy High), and Mary Burns (Martell) addressed the expired teacher contract and fair and equitable compensation; Mrs. Craft also raised teachers not being given steps when they hire in. Ayesha Potts, a Troy resident and District parent, spoke about her candidacy for a seat on the Troy School Board in the upcoming elections.

**Student Representatives**
Jayla Turner (Troy High School), Saanvi Kapu (Athens junior, filling in for Marlien William), and Nurayda Albeez (International Academy-East) reported. Teagan Pruitt (Troy College and Career High School) was not in attendance.

**Board Comments and Announcements**
Dr. Philippart discussed the TSD Business Education Roundtable and the need for interviewers for the 8th Grade Interview Program; Mr. Hauff and Dr. Machesky praised the TSD Art Show at the Troy Community Center. Dates announced: Open-Air Festival Friday, May 17th, 4–9 p.m.; Board Workshop Tuesday, May 7th at 6:00 p.m., Administration Building; next Board Meeting Tuesday, May 21st at 7:00 p.m., Services Building. Mr. Schmidt updated the Board on District–Troy Education Association bargaining and cited the three R's — Recruit, Retain, and Respect.
2024_183_m041624bdmtg.verbose:
Approved minutes of the regular meeting of the Troy Board of Education, Troy, Michigan, held April 16, 2024 at the Troy School District Services Building, 4420 Livernois. President Schmidt called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. In addition to Mr. Schmidt, present were Board members Alic, Anne, Hauff, Haupt, Philippart, and Wilson. Also present were Superintendent Machesky and administrators Montante, DiPilato, Griffor, Smotherman, Keyser, Pagel, Morse, Milanov, Keen, Pawlus, Hall, and West. There were approximately 180 members of the audience. The meeting adjourned at 8:42 p.m., and the minutes were respectfully submitted by Gary N. Hauff, Secretary, Troy Board of Education, with the typist notation GH/jh.

RECOGNITION — TROY SCHOOL DISTRICT'S OUTSTANDING TEACHERS. The Board honored teachers described as having left an indelible mark on students, families, and colleagues, congratulating the Outstanding Teachers of the Year for the 2024 school year. The District received 48 nominations, resulting in the recognition of 41 outstanding teachers. Four of the nominees rose to the top due to their commitment, passion, impact, and dedication to their craft. A short video of the administrative team surprising the winners in their classrooms was shared with the Board and audience. All winners and nominees were recognized at a reception on Tuesday, April 9th at Troy High School, where teachers visited with those who nominated them and all nominees received a certificate, their nomination packets, and a small token of the District's appreciation. The top four winners were invited to the April 16 meeting to be honored, coming to the podium as their names were called to say a few words if they chose and to have their photo taken with members of the Board of Education. The Outstanding Teachers for 2024 are Elizabeth Neuville, Preschool Teacher of the Year, TSD Preschool; Danielle Davenport, Elementary Teacher of the Year, Hill Elementary School; Eric Flessa, High School Teacher of the Year, Troy College & Career High School; and Stephanie Hyska, Middle School Teacher of the Year and overall TSD Teacher of the Year, Boulan Park Middle School. All winners were sent on to Oakland Schools to represent Troy in the Countywide Outstanding Teacher Award program.

MISSION MOMENT — AUTISM ACCEPTANCE MONTH. April has been designated as Autism Acceptance Month. In honor of the month, the Troy School Board of Education acted on a resolution to celebrate the contributions of all neurodiverse people and to work toward ending disparities that autistic people experience when accessing employment, healthcare, and education, recognizing the need for public awareness to promote acceptance, celebrate differences, and be more inclusive toward autistic individuals. It was moved by Dr. Wilson and supported by Mrs. Alic. The whereas clauses stated that Autism Spectrum Disorder affects more than five million people in the United States; that the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention report that 1 in 36 children may have autism; that autism is a neurological and developmental disorder characterized by social impairment and restricted interactive and communication behaviors and can affect anyone regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, or socioeconomic background; that symptoms and characteristics may present in a variety of combinations and can result in significant, lifelong challenges in areas affecting learning, daily living, employment, social-interactive behaviors, and understanding verbal and nonverbal communications; that physicians, psychologists, behavior analysts, speech and language pathologists, occupational therapists, vocational rehabilitation professionals, and educators can assist persons with autism and their families by supporting early identification, education, intervention, recreation, and other opportunities vital to enhanced development and well-being; and that the Troy School District is honored to celebrate the many ways individuals with autism enhance the quality of the school community and is committed to fostering acceptance and a sense of belonging. The resolving clause recognized April 2024 as Autism Acceptance Month in the Troy School District. The vote was Yes: 7, No: 0.

STUDENT SPOTLIGHT. The Board recognized the creative achievements of students in the TSD Creative Guild. Mr. Thomas Butcher returned to present the featured student, Cassandra Wilson, a senior at Athens High School, described as having a familiar face. Butcher spoke about Cassandra and her special work, and Cassandra was invited up to share more about her accomplishments and to receive a certificate of recognition for her creative work.

VOLUNTEER APPRECIATION. The Board extended a thank you to Troy School District volunteers who dedicate their time and talents to the schools and community. In celebration of Volunteer Appreciation Month, the Board expressed gratitude for the contributions of dedicated volunteers whose students will be graduating from TSD this year. Marti Steiner, Peggy Chinoski, Colleen Geyer, and Tara Colussi were invited forward to accept a small token of appreciation for their outstanding service over many years.

ADDITIONS & DELETIONS. None. PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (AGENDA ITEMS). None.

GENERAL — CONSENT AGENDA. It was moved by Mr. Hauff and supported by Mr. Haupt that the Troy Board of Education approve items A, B, C, D, E, and F on the consent agenda: minutes of the March 5, 2024 Special Board of Education Meeting; minutes of the March 5, 2024 Closed Session Meeting; minutes of the March 5, 2024 Board of Education Workshop; minutes of the March 19, 2024 Board of Education Meeting; Treasurer's Report – February 2024; and an Ancillary Fund(s) Budget Amendment. The vote was Yes: 7, No: 0.

PERSONNEL. None. CURRICULUM. None.

BUSINESS — SMITH SWITCH GEAR. It was moved by Mrs. Alic and supported by Dr. Philippart that the bid for the Smith Middle School Switchgear Package be awarded to Great Lakes Power and Lighting in the amount not to exceed $405,000.00, and that this amount be approved as an expenditure of the 2023 Capital Projects Fund. The vote was Yes: 7, No: 0.

PUBLIC COMMUNICATION (NON-AGENDA ITEMS). Mr. Jordan Holsbeke, Martell teacher and 2022 Teacher of the Year, addressed the Board about how Troy values teachers and how they deserve a fair and equitable contract. Mr. Jason Cichowicz, Troy Education Association president, addressed the Board regarding the expired teacher contract, fair and equitable compensation, and the importance of retaining teachers. Ms. Jacqueline Ciolek, Troy High teacher, addressed the expired teacher contract and fair and equitable compensation. Ms. Jennifer Lee, a Larson Middle School teacher of 26 years, addressed the expired teacher contract and fair and equitable compensation. Ms. Heather Kelly, Troy High teacher, addressed the expired teacher contract and fair and equitable compensation. Mrs. Jessica Craft, Troy High teacher, addressed the expired teacher contract, teachers not being given steps when they hire in, and the need for a fair and equitable contract. Mrs. Mary Burns, Martell teacher, addressed the expired teacher contract and fair and equitable compensation. Ayesha Potts, a Troy resident and parent in the District, addressed the Board about her candidacy in running for a seat on the Troy School Board in the upcoming elections.

REPORTS FROM STUDENT REPRESENTATIVES TO THE BOARD. Jayla Turner, student representative for Troy High School, reported on events and activities at her school. Saanvi Kapu, a junior at Athens High School, filled in as student representative because Marlien William was not in attendance, and shared a report on events and activities at Athens. Nurayda Albeez, student representative for International Academy-East, shared a report on events and activities at her school. Teagan Pruitt, student representative for Troy College and Career High School, was not in attendance.

OTHER. None.

BOARD COMMENTS. Dr. Wilson congratulated and thanked the teachers nominated for Teacher of the Year and encouraged participation in the Open-Air Festival, to be held outdoors on Friday, May 17th from 4 to 9 p.m. Dr. Philippart discussed the TSD Business Education Roundtable and the strong partnerships with businesses in the District that have a vested interest in students and schools, and mentioned the need for interviewers for the 8th Grade Interview Program. Mr. Haupt thanked the Teachers of the Year for their dedication and said he enjoyed the video. Mrs. Alic mentioned that the Troy Youth Association is celebrating Volunteer Appreciation Month and that there are opportunities to volunteer in the county, school district, and city. Mr. Hauff encouraged the community to visit the TSD Art Show at the Troy Community Center on Livernois and thanked teachers for supporting and encouraging the fine arts program in TSD. Mrs. Anne thanked the teachers and shared her appreciation of them, and mentioned attending the recent NSBA Conference and visiting schools in that community. Dr. Machesky echoed praise for the TSD Art Show, which he attended the reception for the previous night. Mr. Schmidt also mentioned the NSBA Conference and said the Board would discuss what they learned at the next workshop. He announced that the next Board Workshop would be held Tuesday, May 7th at 6:00 p.m. in the Administration Building and the next Board Meeting Tuesday, May 21st at 7:00 p.m. in the Services Building. He shared a brief update on the status of the District and Teachers Education Association bargaining sessions and mentioned the three R's — Recruit, Retain, and Respect — to sustain the District.

ADJOURNMENT. The meeting adjourned at 8:42 p.m.
